case.case_title: Siriwardena and Others v. Liyanage and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1983] 2 Sri L.R. 164

clause.text: Freedom to engage in lawful occupation or business.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the order sealing the Mahajana Press violated the fundamental right to freedom to engage in any lawful occupation, trade, business or enterprise under Article 14(1)(g) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The proprietors of the Mahajana Press claimed that sealing the press caused loss of business and income, including printing other materials besides the 'Aththa' newspaper, thus violating their fundamental right to engage in lawful occupation and business.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that the principal work of the Mahajana Press was printing the 'Aththa' newspaper, and the order to seal the press was a logical and valid consequence of the order prohibiting publication of the newspaper. The other printing work was trivial in comparison.
key_facts: The Mahajana Press printed the 'Aththa' newspaper and other minor printing jobs.
The press was sealed under the order prohibiting publication of the 'Aththa'.
The press employed 55 employees with significant monthly wages.
Petitioners claimed loss of legitimate income and business due to sealing.
Respondents justified sealing as necessary to enforce the prohibition on publication.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that the order sealing the press was validly made as a necessary consequence of the order prohibiting publication of the 'Aththa' newspaper. Since the principal work of the press was printing the newspaper, the sealing did not violate the fundamental right to engage in lawful occupation or business under Article 14(1)(g).
reasoning.application_to_facts: Given that the main business of the Mahajana Press was printing the 'Aththa' newspaper, and other printing work was trivial, the court found the sealing order reasonable and valid. Therefore, there was no violation of Article 14(1)(g).
principles_established: Freedom to engage in lawful occupation is subject to lawful restrictions.
Sealing a press printing a prohibited publication is a valid enforcement measure.
Incidental impact on other minor business activities does not constitute violation.

outcome.holding: The court held that the order sealing the Mahajana Press was validly made and did not violate the fundamental right to freedom to engage in lawful occupation or business under Article 14(1)(g).

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 14(1)(g) guarantees freedom to engage in lawful occupation or business, which was challenged by the sealing of the press. The court's reasoning addressed whether this restriction was lawful and justified as a consequence of prohibiting the publication.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court noted that the principal work of the Mahajana Press was printing the 'Aththa' newspaper, employing 55 employees with substantial wages, and that other printing work was trivial. The sealing order was therefore a valid consequence of the prohibition on publication.
